## Report: `region_011` (region.fasta, 3,000 bp)

**Summary:** The sequence is not anonymous-looking — it is a protein-coding region containing **two complete genes arranged divergently around a 207-bp intergenic spacer**, and the two genes have **dramatically different synonymous codon usage**, which is the most notable feature of the fragment.

### Region overview
- 3,000 bp, 47.9% GC (A 758 / T 806 / G 701 / C 735); GC varies smoothly from ~40% (5' end) to ~62% (mid) to ~45% (3' end).
- 58% of the fragment (1,734 bp) is protein-coding.

### Feature 1 — orfA: 1161–2177 (+ strand), 338 aa
- ATG at 1161–1163, TAA at 2175–2177 (1,017 nt = 338 codons); previous in-frame stop at 1149–1151, so the 5' end is complete.
- Strongest ORF in the region. Under a mononucleotide-shuffle null (n = 2,000, composition-matched), the longest ORF had median 104 aa, 99th percentile 183 aa, **max 230 aa** — the observed 338 aa was never approached (p < 5×10⁻⁴).
- Decisive coding signature — codon-position GC bias: **GC1/GC2/GC3 = 55.8 / 37.6 / 71.0%** (G-test, G = 77.9, df 2, p ≈ 1×10⁻¹⁷). Genuine genes show silent-site GC enrichment at position 3; random DNA of the same composition would give ~55% at all three positions. The three genuinely non-coding windows of the fragment (1–236, 954–1160, 2178–3000) show no such bias (p = 0.14, 0.14, 0.13).
- Biased codon choice: CTG = 66% of Leu, GCC = 68% of Ala, ACC = 78% of Thr, TAC = 86% of Tyr — typical of a high-GC-genome gene. The gene span is 54.7% GC inside a ~45% GC neighbourhood.
- No Shine-Dalgarno core within the functional 4–13 nt spacing; the nearest purine run (AAGGAAGG, **1127–1134**) lies 26 nt upstream of the start.
- Protein: 338 aa, strongly basic (K+R+H = 61 = 18%, estimated pI > 10), R/Q/E/H-rich, **no transmembrane helices** and no recognizable catalytic motif (checked HExxH, Rossmann GxGxxG, Walker A/B, GxSxG, CxxC, etc.).

### Feature 2 — orfB: 237–953 (− strand), 238 aa
- ATG at 951–953 (minus strand), TGA at 237–239 (717 nt); next in-frame stop upstream at 1014–1016, so the 5' end is also complete.
- Second-longest ORF; the 2nd-longest ORF in the shuffle null never exceeded 215 aa (n = 2,000).
- **Clear Shine-Dalgarno site**: GGAGG core at **958–962**, 4 nt upstream of the ATG — a properly spaced bacterial RBS, which orfA lacks.
- AT-biased third positions: GC1/GC2/GC3 = 46.9 / 47.1 / 36.6% (p = 0.029); codon span 43.5% GC.
- Protein: 238 aa, Ala/Thr/Gly/Ser-rich, low charged fraction, no TM helices, no motifs.

### Feature 3 — Gene architecture (954–1160)
The two genes point away from each other: orfB (←, 237–953) and orfA (→, 1161–2177) share a 207-bp divergent intergenic region. It contains −35-like hexamers (TTGAC at **1082–1086**; TGACA on the minus strand at **996–992**) but no canonical −35(17–19 nt)−10 pairing, so no promoter could be called confidently.

### Notable observation
The two adjacent genes use **incompatible synonymous codon sets** (GC3 = 71% vs 37%; synonymous-usage G-test G = 110, df 38, p < 10⁻¹⁰) and differ in translation-initiation signals (SD present/absent). Two genes with such contrasting silent-site composition and codon choice within one 3-kb window is the classic footprint of genes with different ancestry — e.g., a native gene plus a horizontally acquired one. Only sequence-intrinsic evidence is available here, so this is an inference, not an identification.

### Nothing else stood out (negative results)
- No repeats: no exact direct repeats ≥18 bp, no tandem repeats ≥15 bp/3 units, no CRISPR-like arrays, no long homopolymers (max 6-mer, six occurrences).
- No tRNA-like motifs, no DnaA-box/chi-site signatures, ordinary restriction-site counts.
- Only one perfect inverted repeat ≥7-bp stem: **2854–2874** (AGATAGT / 7-nt loop / ACTATCT) — weak, no terminator-like U-run.
- No rho-independent terminator found downstream of either gene (best weak candidates: 2363–2377 and 975–994).
- All other ORFs ≥90 aa are either nested internal start codons of these two genes (they share the same stops at 2175–2177 or 237–239) or, in the case of the 161-aa minus-strand ORF at 2215–2700 (and its nested starts), show no codon-position bias (p = 0.84) and are most likely chance ORFs. Minus-strand ORFs overlapping orfA (e.g., 1473–1841) reflect the positional structure of the coding frame and are not separate genes.

**Caveats:** All analysis is sequence-intrinsic (composition, frame statistics, ORF significance, motif patterns, regulatory signals); no database/homology search was possible, so no functional assignment is made. The fragment is 3 kb with unknown flanking context, so terminators/promoters for these genes may lie outside it.
